title: China drafts export controls on frontier AI models, agents and compute clusters
summary: On October 16 China's commerce and science ministries (MOFCOM Announcement No. 48) proposed adding 40 technologies to the export ban/restriction catalogue, 23 of them AI: large models above 10^26 training FLOPs, over 2T parameters or world top-10 capability (weights, checkpoints, architecture), big multi-agent and tool-calling agent systems, and compute clusters. Comments are open until November 15, but pre-export registration already applies. Technology already public via open source or papers is excluded, and API or SaaS access is not treated as export, so this is not an automatic end to Chinese open weights.
author: phox
quip: 🇨🇳📦 Beijing puts frontier weights on the export list. Open-source carve-out is the whole ballgame, read the fine print before you panic 🧐
image_caption: China drafts export controls on frontier AI models, agents and compute clusters

title: GLM-5.3-Flash joins DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as a free model in OpenCode
summary: OpenCode made GLM-5.3-Flash free on October 16 (model id glm-5.3-flash-free), right after the free DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Limits: 200K context and 32K max output on the free GLM route versus 1M/131K paid, it only works inside OpenCode (outside API calls get a 403 FreeTierError), quotas are unpublished and users report slowdowns under load. An independent test pushed about 1.04M tokens through the free DeepSeek route, hinting the 200K cap is client-side. No end date announced.
author: phox
quip: 🆓🤖 Two free Flash models in one week. OpenCode is speedrunning customer acquisition, this is the way 🏃
image_caption: GLM-5.3-Flash joins DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as a free model in OpenCode

title: BigMoeOnEdge v0.29: stream MoE experts from storage to run giant models on a 12GB phone
summary: BigMoeOnEdge, an open-source engine on stock llama.cpp, streams MoE experts from storage so models far bigger than RAM run on-device; the 4PDA post cites 120B-class MoE on a 12GB phone and Gemma 4 26B-A4B at about 4 tok/s (developer claims, not independently checked). The v0.29.0 release adds an --auto hardware planner, a desktop app with an OpenAI-compatible local server, and a macOS port with Metal.
author: ENA21
quip: 📱🐘 120B on a phone via SSD streaming. 4 tok/s is slow but it's YOUR 4 tok/s. Benchmarks or it didn't happen 👀
image_caption: BigMoeOnEdge v0.29: stream MoE experts from storage to run giant models on a 12GB phone

title: Unofficial native OpenCode port for Android ships with a built-in Linux shell
summary: A new unofficial port packs an OpenCode server, its web UI and a working Linux terminal into a single Android APK, with no root and nothing else to install. The forum poster pitches it as better than existing OpenCode mobile wrappers; the repo appeared on October 16 and builds are hash-pinned.
author: tixyq
quip: 🤳💻 Coding agent in your pocket, terminal included. Pair it with the free Flash models and vibe-code on the bus 🚌
image_caption: Unofficial native OpenCode port for Android ships with a built-in Linux shell

title: qwen-colab-book-gen: free-tier Google Colab pipeline turns books into Qwen audiobooks
summary: An alpha open-source tool where a Telegram bot takes a book and runs audiobook generation with Qwen TTS on Google Colab's free tier via the Colab CLI, saving the result to Google Drive. Shipped as a Docker image; early and rough, posted in 4PDA's TTS club.

title: MOSS-Image: OpenMOSS open-sources a 5B image model that places text and objects by bounding box
summary: OpenMOSS released MOSS-Image on October 16 with Base and SFT checkpoints under Apache-2.0: a 5B DiT that renders English and Chinese text and takes a JSON layout where you place text and objects by bounding box, so editing one caption or box changes only that part. ComfyUI added same-day support; repacked weights are 10.2 GB in bf16 or 5.4 GB in int8.

title: Meta's Muse Spark Open: 816B-A42B open weights for coding agents, runs on two Mac Studios
summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open on October 15 and calls it the most capable US open-weight model to date: a natively multimodal MoE with 816B total and 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context, built for coding and agent work. Weights in BF16 and NVFP4 are on Hugging Face under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms; Meta says it runs locally on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX, and llama.cpp, vLLM and SGLang support it.

quip: 🧠🔓 816B open weights from Meta. Hope you've got two Mac Studios and a spare kidney 💸 GGUFs or it didn't happen 👀

title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017: open-weight update with cheaper agent runs and a public Search API
summary: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash-1017 on October 17 with MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope, and it now serves the deepseek-flash API name. DeepSeek's own benchmarks show DeepSWE v1.1 rising from 74.2 to 77.0 at just under $0.20 per task, with shorter outputs. Its in-house Search and Fetch APIs are now open to all developers at $0.75 per 1,000 calls. Independent benchmarks aren't out yet.
author: Leostrange
quip: 🐋💸 77 on DeepSWE for twenty cents a task, per DeepSeek's own chart. Independent evals or it didn't happen 🧐

title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5: Super VL 120B-A12B and a 2-bit Bolt model that fits in 24 GB
summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 on October 15. Super VL is an open 120B-parameter MoE (12B active) Mamba-Transformer hybrid that reads text, images and video with up to 1M tokens of context. Bolt 74B-A9B is compressed from it and natively quantized to about 2 bits to fit in 24 GB for local agents, with a speculative-decoding drafter and a reported 84 tokens/s on RTX Spark. Both use the OpenMDW-1.1 license.
author: Leostrange
quip: 🟩🗜️ 74B squeezed to 2 bits so it fits a 24 GB card. Your 3090 just got a second wind 🔥
image_caption: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5: Super VL 120B-A12B and a 2-bit Bolt model that fits in 24 GB

title: Elorian Glimpse: a vision model that re-checks images and video while it reasons
summary: Elorian released its first model, Glimpse, on October 16 as a research preview through its API and chat. Instead of describing an image once, it goes back mid-reasoning to crop regions, rewatch video at denser frame rates, track objects and measure details with code. It costs $0.60 per million input tokens and $3 per million output tokens, and it's already on OpenRouter and Vercel's AI Gateway.
author: Leostrange
quip: 👁️🔍 A model that actually looks twice before answering. More than most Redditors do 😏
image_caption: Elorian Glimpse: a vision model that re-checks images and video while it reasons

title: Tencent Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: a small open model that just writes agent memory
summary: Tencent Hunyuan open-sourced Hy-Memory-30B-A3B on October 15, a MoE with about 3B active parameters that replaces the general LLM in the write path of memory frameworks like Mem0, MemOS and Hy-Memory, deciding what to keep and how to update it. In Tencent's own tests across four memory harnesses it averages 55.49 versus 54.62 for Claude Opus 5; weights and an FP8 variant are on Hugging Face.
author: Leostrange
quip: 🧠📝 A dedicated memory scribe for your agent. Finally something that remembers your preferences 🗃️
image_caption: Tencent Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: a small open model that just writes agent memory

title: Non-programmer builds Black Tank, an online 3D tank game, with Claude in about six months
summary: A 4PDA user who says he isn't a programmer spent about six months building Black Tank, an online 3D tank game with Counter-Strike-style team battles and long upgrade progression, by working with AI. After moving from Gemini to ChatGPT to Claude, he first built a browser version with Claude Opus 4.6, then in September used Opus 5.5 to rewrite the client in Godot. Android and browser players share the same battles, and he says the new version runs about 3x faster.
author: iyong
quip: 🎮🛡️ Six months of vibe-coding and it's a real multiplayer tank game in Godot. This is the way 🫡
